cities.base: Midtown or downtown Anchorage, close to the airport for the bookend nights
cities.name: Anchorage

cities.base: Downtown Seward near the small boat harbor, walkable to the waterfront and close to the Kenai Fjords dock
cities.name: Seward

cities.base: day trip from Healy / Carlo Creek
cities.name: Savage River / Savage Alpine Trail

cities.base: day trip from Healy / Carlo Creek via park shuttle
cities.name: Eielson Visitor Center area

places.name: Denali Visitor Center
places.note: Free exhibits on the park's wildlife and geology, good stop on your way in to get oriented and check trail conditions before driving out to Savage River. Skip if you're tight on time, it's not essential.

places.name: Marmot Meadows (Harding Icefield Trail overlook, mile 1)
places.note: About a mile up the Harding Icefield Trail, first real overlook with glacier and valley views. Good turnaround point if you want a taste of the trail without committing to the full 8 miles.

places.name: Resurrection River Overlook
places.note: Short pullout view of the braided river below the glacier. Not a destination on its own, worth thirty seconds if you are already at the trailhead.

places.name: Exit Glacier Road
places.note: Nine miles of paved road from the Seward Highway to the glacier trailhead, with moose in the cottonwoods along the Resurrection River. It is unplowed and closed to cars from about October to May, so in November it is a ski or a walk.

places.name: Exit Glacier Nature Center
places.note: Free. A small ranger station with glacier retreat maps, open only from Memorial Day weekend to Labor Day, so it is shut in November and the road to it is closed to cars. In season the rangers know trail and ice closures better than any app.

places.name: Humpy's Great Alaskan Alehouse
places.note: Loud, touristy, but a solid last-night option for beer and bar food within walking distance of downtown hotels.

places.name: Side Street Espresso
places.note: Small local coffee spot a block off the main drag, good option before a museum morning.

places.name: Anchorage Downtown Saturday Market
places.note: Runs Saturdays and Sundays mid-May through mid-September only, closed the rest of the week. Food stalls and local vendors, fine for an hour if your bookend day lands on a weekend.

places.name: Lake Hood Seaplane Base
places.note: Busiest floatplane base in the world, constant takeoffs and landings. Quick, free, genuinely distinct to Anchorage.

places.name: Earthquake Park
places.note: 134 acres on the ground the 1964 quake tore up, magnitude 9.2 and four minutes long, with interpretive signs and Cook Inlet and skyline views. Open 06:00 to 23:00, check the price (a visitor calls it free, with free parking). Thirty minutes off the Coastal Trail.

places.name: Snow City Cafe
places.note: The downtown breakfast everyone queues for on weekends; plates run about $5 to $18. Hours vary, check: its own site says 07:00 to 15:00 daily, another listing gives weekends to 16:00. Eat here before a driving day.

places.name: Glacier BrewHouse
places.note: Reliable dinner near the hotels downtown, good for a first or last night when you don't want to think hard about where to eat.

places.name: Beluga Point
places.note: Roadside turnout at Mile 110 of the Seward Highway over Turnagain Arm, where belugas sometimes show and the tidal bore runs if your timing is right. Stay off the mudflats and the railway line. No fee is posted, check the price. A 20 minute stop.

places.name: Anchorage Museum
places.note: Opened 1968. $25 adult, $20 Alaska residents, under 6 free, and free on First Fridays 18:00 to 21:00. October to April it opens Tuesday to Saturday 10:00 to 18:00 and Sunday from 12:00, shut Mondays. Skip it only if the Heritage Center already took your day.

places.name: Tony Knowles Coastal Trail
places.note: Paved trail along the inlet, good for stretching legs before a flight. Watch for moose, they do turn up.

places.name: Alaska Native Heritage Center
places.note: Opened 1999 and run by Alaska Native people. Winter is Monday to Friday 09:00 to 17:00 with a suggested $10 donation, summer adult entry was $30 in 2025; the 2026-27 season is not posted yet, so check the price and the hours before you drive out.

places.name: Savage River / Savage Alpine Trail
places.note: Free, no shuttle needed, good if the full Eielson day feels like too much sitting.

places.name: Denali shuttle to Eielson Visitor Center
places.note: Reservation required, book the second you have dates; private vehicles can't go past mile 15.

places.name: Exit Glacier
places.note: Free, Kenai Fjords charges no entrance fee. The road is unplowed and closed to cars from about October to May, so in November you ski or walk in. In season do it the afternoon you arrive, not the morning after the boat tour.

places.name: Kenai Fjords boat tour dock
places.note: Closed now: no full-day cruise runs past September 20. The 8.5 hour Northwestern Fjord cruise is $329 for 2027, May 28 to Sep 6, against $259 for 6 hours; the longer one is the difference between maybe seeing a glacier calve and seeing one.

places.name: Outwash Plain Trail
places.note: Flat gravel loop across the gray outwash plain in front of the glacier. Good for kids or anyone who wants glacier views without climbing, but it is exposed with no shade and can be windy.

places.name: Exit Glacier Campground
places.note: Walk-in tent sites near the road, no vehicle access to sites. Only relevant if camping rather than staying in Seward, and bear canisters are required, this is active bear country.

places.name: Exit Glacier Road junction pullout, Seward Highway
places.note: The turnoff itself, easy to miss if you are moving fast. Not a place to linger, just noting it so the drive in does not get missed.

places.name: Exit Glacier guided ice walk (private operator, seasonal)
places.note: Crampons and a guide onto the actual ice, run by outfitters based in Seward, not the park service. Only worth it if you have not done a proper glacier walk elsewhere in Alaska already, otherwise it is a lot of money for something the free trail already shows you from a safe distance.

places.name: Exit Glacier viewing platform crowds (midday)
places.note: Skip going at midday in July, tour buses from Seward stack the parking lot and the short trail gets crowded. Same view at 8am or after 5pm with a fraction of the people.

places.name: Exit Glacier area flightseeing (skip, use Talkeetna instead)
places.note: Some Seward operators sell flightseeing over Exit Glacier and the Harding Icefield. Skip it here, the Denali/Talkeetna flightseeing already planned covers this better and doing both is redundant spending on the same kind of splurge.

places.name: Savage River Loop Trail
places.note: 1.7 mile flat loop along both banks of the Savage River, crosses two footbridges. No elevation gain, good for the day you don't want a strenuous hike. Furthest point you can drive a private car into the park, so no shuttle needed.

places.name: Savage Alpine Trail
places.note: 4 miles point to point between the Savage River parking area and Mountain Vista, about 1500 ft elevation gain, 3-4 hours if you do it one way and arrange a shuttle back, longer if you go out and back. Real alpine tundra views without needing the bus system. Exposed ridge, turn back if wind picks up.

places.name: Savage River Trailhead / Mile 15 Parking Area
places.note: The actual starting point, has restrooms and a small ranger contact station in summer. This is the hard stop for private vehicles on the park road, everything past here needs the shuttle.

places.name: Mountain Vista Picnic Area / Alpine Trail East Trailhead
places.note: The other end of the Alpine Trail, has picnic tables and pit toilets. Shuttle buses stop here, useful if you want to do the Alpine Trail one direction only.

places.name: Savage River Footbridge
places.note: Midpoint crossing of the loop trail, good spot to watch for Dall sheep on the slopes above and to turn back early if you're short on time.

places.name: Savage River Dall Sheep Viewing Area
places.note: Steep canyon walls just south of the parking area are a reliable spot for Dall sheep with binoculars, no guarantee but good odds in early morning.

places.name: Igloo Canyon Pullout
places.note: Only reachable by shuttle, past the Savage checkpoint, but a known spot for grizzly and Dall sheep sightings if your bus stops here on the way to Eielson. Not a standalone destination, mention to the driver if you want a photo stop.

places.name: Savage River Campground
places.note: The last drive-in campground in the park, worth a stop even if you're not camping, decent base for an early start on the Alpine Trail since it's right by the Mountain Vista end.

places.name: Primrose Ridge
places.note: Unmaintained route straight up the tundra slope near the Savage River check station, steep and no trail, good if you want solitude and are comfortable off-trail hiking. Not for anyone who wants a marked path.

places.name: Sanctuary River Area
places.note: Past the Savage River checkpoint, requires the shuttle or a permit. Off-trail river bar walking, quieter than Savage River itself, only worth it if you've already done the shuttle day and want more.

places.name: Murie Science and Learning Center
places.note: Denali's winter visitor center from mid-September to mid-May, so it is the one open now, 09:00 to 16:00. No entry fee is stated, check the price; rangers sell the park entrance pass here, credit card only. Thin for a casual visitor.

places.name: Simon & Seafort's Saloon & Grill
places.note: Downtown seafood and steak grill: fish and chips $24, prime rib French dip $23, almond crusted scallops $42 on the current menu. Open daily 11:30 to 21:00, though one listing says to 22:00 Monday to Saturday, so check.

places.name: The Highliner Restaurant
places.note: The Seward restaurant that stays open through winter. Cod and chips $29, halibut and chips $39, burger $18. Hours vary, check: 12:00 to 20:00 weekdays and from 11:00 at weekends on its ordering page, later on another listing.

places.name: Flamingo Lounge
places.note: Open year round but shut Monday to Wednesday: dinner 17:00 to 20:45 Thursday to Sunday, plus lunch 11:00 to 13:45 at weekends. Rockfish $30, salmon $34, halibut chowder from $8.

places.name: Woody's Thai Kitchen
places.note: Thai, open year round, about $25 a head on one listing (no menu price seen). Hours vary, check: listings range from Tuesday to Saturday 12:00 to 20:00 to six days a week, so call 907-422-0338. Long waits when a cruise ship is in.

places.name: Alaska SeaLife Center
places.note: Alaska's only permanent marine mammal rehab center, with sea lions and puffins and a free audio tour (bring earbuds). Winter, Oct 1 to Mar 3, is Thursday to Monday 12:00 to 17:00; adult about $32. Book online, entry times sell out.

places.name: Seward Community Library & Museum
places.note: Seward's history with the Resurrection Bay Historical Society. Free October to April, open only Friday 10:00 to 18:00 and Saturday to 17:00. Summer is $5 cash with the 1964 quake film daily at 14:00; summer hours are not posted, so call 907-224-3902. 45 minutes.

places.name: Iditarod Historic Trail Statue, Mile 0
places.note: Mile 0 of the Iditarod Historic Trail, the gold-rush route the sled race later took: a prospector and his dog in bronze. Founder's Monument on the south-east waterfront marks the 1903 landing. No fee posted, check the price. Twenty minutes by the SeaLife Center.
places.neighborhood: Railway Ave, by the SeaLife Center

places.name: Benny Benson Memorial Park
places.note: For Benny Benson, the 13 year old Alutiiq boy who designed the Alaska flag. A boardwalk over a lagoon with eagles, otters and birds, open all hours; no fee posted, check the price.

places.name: Mt Marathon Trailhead
places.note: The town's demanding hike straight up from 1st Avenue. Hikers say it is snow-free only from mid to late June, so in November it is snow and ice and not one to try. No fee posted, check the price.

places.name: Two Lakes Park
places.note: An easy low forest loop around two lakes at the foot of Mt Marathon, the walk to do when the mountain is iced over. Hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Kenai Fjords National Park Visitor Center
places.note: Free, the park charges no entrance fee. Open only from Memorial Day weekend to Labor Day, about 08:30 to 19:00, so it is closed in November; in season stop here before the boat for the park film and current conditions.

places.name: Lowell Point State Recreation Site
places.note: A beach south of town and the start of the Tonsina Point trail, 4.2 miles out and back and walkable year round. Hours and any fee are not posted, check the price.

places.name: Alaska Aviation Museum
places.note: Opened 1988 after a fire destroyed the old transport museum's planes. See the Grumman Goose flown again in 2024 and the 1962 Merrill Field tower cab. $23, 90 minutes, no booking; 10:00 to 17:00 in winter, Sundays vary by month, check. Pair with Lake Hood.

places.name: Alaska Veterans Museum
places.note: Alaska's soldiers from the Civil War to now: weapons, uniforms, a research library and the bronze Last Blue Whale. $5, an hour. Labor Day to Memorial Day it opens Wednesday to Saturday 10:00 to 17:00, summer Monday to Saturday. Upstairs; the elevator needs a booked visit.

places.name: Holy Family Cathedral
places.note: Parish founded 1915; the wooden church was damaged by an earthquake and rebuilt in Romanesque Revival style in 1946, now a co-cathedral. Free, 20 minutes. Visiting hours outside services are not posted: weekday Mass runs 11:00 to 13:15, so go just after.

places.name: Eklutna Historical Park
places.note: Old St Nicholas, built about 1870, is the oldest standing building around Anchorage, beside Dena'ina spirit houses over the graves. Closed now: guided tours run 15 May to 15 Sep, weekdays 10:00 to 17:00. Check the price. 90 minutes, 40 km north-east.

places.name: St Peter's Episcopal Church
places.note: Consecrated in 1906, Seward's first wooden church when the others were tents. The thing to see is the 1925 Resurrection reredos by Dutch painter Jan Van Empel. Free, 20 minutes; hours are not posted and it may be locked in winter, so check.

places.name: Van Gilder Hotel
places.note: Built in 1916 as offices and a hotel since 1921; the 1924 Army round-the-world flight crew stayed here after landing in Resurrection Bay. Still a working hotel, so a free 15 minute look at the outside; lobby hours not posted.

places.name: Brown & Hawkins Store
places.note: Opened 1903-04 to supply the Alaska Central Railroad crews, long Seward's oldest running business. The owners announced retirement in 2013 with no buyer, so it may not trade now: free to look at from the street, 15 minutes.

places.name: Caines Head State Recreation Area
places.note: Holds Fort McGilvray, a WWII coastal fort begun 1941 and dismantled 1944, concrete still standing. 4.5 miles from Lowell Point; the beach past Tonsina passes only at very low tide, leave 2 hours before it. Free, $5 parking. A full day, not one for November.

outings.why: The 8.5-hour version is the difference between maybe seeing a glacier calve and definitely seeing one, but weather cancels these more than people expect so don't book a flight home the same day.
outings.name: Kenai Fjords boat tour
outings.season: late May to early September (8.5 hour cruise May 28 to Sep 6
outings.fallback: Exit Glacier's easy 1-2 hour trail if the boat is scrubbed.

outings.why: 1-2 hours round trip on an easy trail, do it the afternoon you arrive in Seward, not the wrecked morning after the boat tour. The road is closed to cars from about October to May.
outings.name: Exit Glacier hike

outings.why: 6-8 hours round trip depending how far you go, the only way past mile 15 since private vehicles are barred; the mountain itself is visible only about 30% of days even in summer.
outings.name: Denali park shuttle toward Eielson Visitor Center
outings.fallback: Savage River / Savage Alpine Trail if the full shuttle day feels like too much sitting.

outings.why: 2-4 hours, free, no shuttle needed, the lighter alternative to the full Eielson day.
outings.name: Savage River / Savage Alpine Trail

outings.why: 1-1.5 hours air time, only worth booking if your itinerary has slack for a weather delay since these get scrubbed constantly; don't stack it with the boat tour unless money's no object.
outings.name: Denali flightseeing

destination.name: Alaska (Anchorage / Seward / Denali)
destination.pitch: Pick fjords and tundra, not the whole state — Anchorage as a bookend, Seward for ocean wildlife, Denali for the interior, and accept that both headline days are weather lotteries.
destination.caveat: Two of your six nights are mostly car time, and both headline experiences, the fjords boat tour and the Denali summit, are weather lotteries you don't control. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.nature: Kenai Fjords puts you in front of calving glaciers and marine wildlife in one long boat day, and Denali gives you tundra and a 20-million-acre park to look at.
because.culture: The Alaska Native Heritage Center in Anchorage is a solid two to three hours if you want it, though the trip isn't built around culture.
because.adventure: The Seward Highway drive, the fjords boat, and the Denali shuttle toward Eielson are all full-day pushes, not strolls.
because.exploration: Denali's road is closed to private cars past mile 15, so getting to Eielson on the shuttle feels like actually getting into the interior, not just driving past it.
